editorial.headline: Private Screen Production: Open Nationally, Scope-Dependent in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A broad private production activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali PMA registration turns on the exact declared scope and its OSS risk.
editorial.body:
Private film, video and television production is the paid, privately managed making of moving-image work. The scope is deliberately broad: films, videos and audiovisual works—including 2D, 3D and stop-motion animation, or combinations of those techniques—sit beside television programmes, moving television advertisements and television news programmes. It also expressly includes vlogs and video podcasts produced under private management for remuneration. Sports-media content made as film, video or TV, films produced for television screening, film-delivery services and film booking-agency work are all part of the same stated activity.

Its edges matter. The record separates this production activity from duplicating films or reproducing audio or video recordings from a master onto CDs, DVDs or other physical media. It also excludes animation post-production. In practical terms, the classification follows the creation and production of moving-image material, alongside the specified delivery and booking services; it should not be stretched to claim the distinct physical-copying or animation-post-production work outside its stated boundary.

The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with maximum foreign ownership of 100%. This is a national foreign-ownership ceiling, not a partial one: a foreign investor may hold the full stake permitted by that ceiling in a business confined to this scope. It is the cleanest part of the picture, grounded in the listed national source. The scale list establishes who may register; it does not turn every individual element of the production scope into the same Bali registration outcome.

Bali is where precision becomes decisive. The record does not mark the activity as universally blocked for PMA; its Bali status is scope-dependent. At Besar scale, OSS treats some stated scopes as low risk and others as higher risk. Bali permanently blocks PMA registration island-wide for all low- and medium-low-risk activities. The activity can be registered as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope. A founder should therefore verify the exact activity live in OSS before treating the national 100% ceiling as a Bali registration result. No separate Bali ownership percentage or partnership condition is stated here; Bali’s distinction is the declared scope’s risk position.
editorial.pullQuote: The activity can be registered as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope.
